newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rebels pound government-held town.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rebels pound government-held town.

text.p: Tamil Tiger rebels shelled the government-held frontline town of Vavuniya in northern Sri Lanka early on Saturday, killing two policemen in their barracks, residents said.

It was the first use of long-range artillery by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) guerrillas against Vavuniya, a strategic town from where government forces last Tuesday launched their biggest offensive so far this year.
The government immediately responded to the LTTE battery with an attack by helicopters and air force bombers.
Incoming shells began pounding Vavuniya shortly after midnight, residents said. A Defence Ministry spokesman confirmed the shelling but had no further details.
"Altogether, we must have heard about 20 explosions, but did not see that much damage done by them," said a resident who asked not to be named.
The LTTE, fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese nation, appear to have been aiming at police and army barracks, the residents said.
One said he saw a shell strike the police barracks and later saw the bodies of two dead policemen. Two buses were also damaged.
The LTTE artillery also hit two Sinhalese villages to the southeast of Vavuniya, but there were no known casualties, the residents said.
Military officials in Vavuniya were not available for comment. The LTTE has remained silent about the shelling.

In this week's government offensive, the army, led by elite units and supported by tanks and aircraft, had advanced 22 km (14 miles) out of Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, by Friday, the Defence Ministry said.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the 14-year old conflict. The LTTE says the toll is much higher.
